findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

The attestation meets the executable-red requirements. The exact attested command exited 1 with no signal and no timeout. The expected literal "Human refusal must name the fixed observation recovery command" appears in full stdout, and stdout is not truncated. The failure comes from the assert.ok at line 38 of bounded-observation-human.node.ts, which is the recovery-command check. Every earlier check passed: no spawn error, exit status 2, "Execution-only", the exact changed file, and "commit or clean". So the RED is not caused by syntax, imports, fixtures or environment. The proof runs the scenario's actor-facing When: the real public CLI runs `proof observe-bounded-delivery` in human mode on a disposable committed candidate with an uncommitted proof configuration edit. It then reads the actor-visible refusal text. The rendered output names the changed input and asks to commit or clean, but it offers only a verify command for the refused attempt. It never names the fixed observation request. That is the intended missing human-rendering recovery behavior. The assertions that come after the failure point (exactly one observe command, no verify command offered as recovery, and the changed-input diagnostic printed once) will also discriminate during GREEN. The current output prints that diagnostic twice. I found no blocking errors.

This human proof never checks the scenario's first Then, "no proof execution starts". The packet says the JSON dirty-input control covers that. In this human path, an implementation could start the runner and still render the same refusal text. Consider asserting that no runner report or log artifact exists, or that the attempt never reached the running stage, so this proof checks both Then clauses on its own.

Line 1 of the test disables vitest/no-import-node-test with the comment "This real human-output preflight never starts a test runner." That claim is wrong: the file imports node:test, and the observer is designed to launch Vitest. The suppression may be fine, but the justification should be corrected.

The rule against `safeword proof verify-bounded-delivery` (assert.equal(message.includes(...), false)) bans the verify command anywhere in the output, not just as the offered recovery action. The plan also requires refusals to name a retained attempt reference when one exists. GREEN must keep the attempt ID visible while dropping the verify suggestion. That is achievable, but the assertion is broader than the stated intent.

The attested Node version is v24.3.0, while the plan pins v24.18.1. The test doesn't depend on that pin, because it refuses before tool resolution matters, so the RED is unaffected. Real-run success proofs will still need the pinned toolchain.

The recovery-command requirement comes from the plan's CLI surface and persona contract (one concrete recovery action) and the ledger's plan-to-scenario trace. The scenario wording only asks for a committed clean candidate. I am accepting it as related behavior at the same actor boundary, consistent with prior review 88816ba2.
